translations.literal: Ma Guanghui (Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner. In the eighth year of Tiancong, for surrendering in submission granted third-class jalan janggin. For cause reduced to niru janggin. By military merit raised to first-class jalan janggin. At duty evaluation granted half rank of advancement. For cause, reduced and granted baitalaburu hafan. By grace edict added one tūsaḥa hafan. When the matter was cleared, promoted to first-class ada-ha hafan plus one tūsaḥa hafan. In the first month of the ninth year of Shunzhi, by grace edict raised to third-class ashan-i hafan. Now rendered in Chinese as third-class baron. Died. Posthumous title Zhongjing.)
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guanghui (Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner; in Tiancong 8 he surrendered and received third-class jalan janggin. He was reduced to niru janggin for cause, then military merit raised him to first-class jalan janggin. At duty evaluation he received half rank of advancement, but for cause was reduced and granted baitalaburu hafan; a grace edict added one tūsaḥa hafan. When the matter was cleared he was promoted to first-class ada-ha hafan plus one tūsaḥa hafan, and a grace edict in the first month of Shunzhi 9 raised him to third-class ashan-i hafan, now recorded in Chinese as third-class baron. He died and was given the posthumous title Zhongjing.)

translations.literal: Tan-bu (Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner. In the fifth year of Chongde, for military merit granted niru janggin. Soon raised to first-class ada-ha hafan plus one tūsaḥa hafan. For cause stripped of tūsaḥa hafan. By grace edict added one tūsaḥa hafan. In the second month of the eighth year of Shunzhi, by military merit raised to third-class ashan-i hafan. In the first month of the ninth year, by grace edict raised to second class. For cause reduced to first-class ada-ha hafan plus one tūsaḥa hafan. Again met a grace edict, raised to third-class ashan-i hafan. Now rendered in Chinese as third-class baron.)

translations.literal: Hu Yisheng (Native of Changsha in Hunan. In the second year of Tongzhi, as Brigade Commander of Huai-Yang, for merit in recovering Suzhou he was granted Cloud Cavalry Commandant. In the seventh year, when Zhang Zongyu was pacified, granted one more Cloud Cavalry Commandant, combined as third-class baron. Died in the tenth year of Guangxu while serving as Yangtze Naval Commander-in-Chief. Posthumous title Wujing.)

translations.literal: Peng Yuju (Native of Xiangxiang in Hunan. Registered as Provincial Administration Commissioner. In the third year of Tongzhi, for merit in taking Jinling he was granted first-class Commandant of Light Chariot. Soon appointed Circuit Intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long in Fujian. In the second month of the sixth year of Tongzhi, while suppressing the Eastern Nian, he fell in battle at Qishui in Hubei. Posthumously granted Grand Secretary, posthumous title Zhongzhuang, and Commandant of Cavalry. Soon combined as third-class baron.)
